name: Draw App — Excalidraw in Svelte
shortDescription: Full-stack whiteboard app embedding Excalidraw's React component inside Svelte with auth and persistent workspaces.
longDescription: A full-stack whiteboard application built with SvelteKit, embedding Excalidraw's React component within a Svelte app to demonstrate cross-framework integration. Features user authentication (email/password + GitHub OAuth via Better Auth), persistent canvas storage with PostgreSQL and Drizzle ORM, folder organization, and transactional emails with Resend. React is initialized inside a Svelte 5 $effect() via the @attach directive, making it active only within that single component lifecycle while the rest of the app is pure Svelte.
highlights: Cross-framework integration: React component inside Svelte 5
User auth with email/password + GitHub OAuth via Better Auth
Persistent workspaces with PostgreSQL + Drizzle ORM
Transaction emails (verification, password reset) via Resend
Lazy-loaded React rendering isolated from Svelte runtime

name: Anime Database
shortDescription: Next.js anime and manga database powered by the AniList GraphQL API, styled with Tailwind CSS, with i18n and favorites.
longDescription: An application built with Next.js that connects to the AniList API using GraphQL to display detailed information about anime and manga. Features include browsing by genre, popularity, and release dates, an integrated search bar, a favorites section persisted in Local Storage, and a global language switcher (English/Spanish) that stores user preference across sessions.
highlights: Client-side favorites persisted in Local Storage
Global language switcher (EN/ES) with persistent preference
Advanced search and filtering for anime and manga

name: Netflix Clone
shortDescription: Netflix clone built with Svelte and SvelteKit, developed as a learning project with custom implementation.
longDescription: A Netflix clone built with Svelte and SvelteKit. Developed while following a Udemy course, but implemented with my own approach and design decisions. Covers component composition, routing, and responsive layouts in SvelteKit.

name: CSS Web Animations Gallery
shortDescription: Curated collection of CSS, SVG, and GSAP animation techniques built with SvelteKit.
longDescription: A visual gallery and learning resource demonstrating various web animation techniques including pure CSS transitions, keyframes, clip-paths, SVG path animations, and GSAP ScrollTrigger effects. Built with SvelteKit to organize multiple animation categories with a floating navigation menu.
highlights: Pure CSS transitions, keyframes, and clip-path effects
Floating navigation across multiple animation categories

name: Blue Archive Database
shortDescription: My first React project -- a character database for browsing Blue Archive data.
longDescription: One of my earliest projects and my first time building with React. A frontend app built with TypeScript and Vite that loads character data from a local JSON file. Simple but meaningful -- it's where I learned React component architecture and state management.

name: Vue Notes App
shortDescription: Vue.js notes app with register/login, CRUD notes, and admin mode, connected to a Hono backend.
longDescription: Vue.js frontend for a notes application. Features user registration and login, full CRUD for notes with title and description, and an admin mode to view and delete other users. Connects to a separate Hono backend deployed on Cloudflare Workers.
highlights: CRUD notes with title and description

name: Hono Notes Backend
shortDescription: Hono REST API backend for the Vue notes app, deployed on Cloudflare Workers with Drizzle ORM.
longDescription: Backend API built with Hono running on Cloudflare Workers. Provides REST endpoints for user authentication, note CRUD operations, and admin user management. Uses Drizzle ORM for database access and Bun as the local development runtime.

name: Blue Archive Wiki Scraper
shortDescription: C# console application that scrapes and structures data from the Blue Archive Wiki.
longDescription: A console application built with C# and .NET that crawls the Blue Archive Wiki to extract and structure character and game data. Uses HtmlAgilityPack with XPath to parse and extract HTML content, Entity Framework with SQLite for data persistence, and dependency injection for service management.
highlights: HtmlAgilityPack with XPath for HTML parsing
Entity Framework with SQLite for data persistence
Structured data output from unstructured wiki content

name: Simple Anime Gallery
shortDescription: Vanilla JS image gallery searching anime images via the yande.re API. *(archived — API no longer works client-side)*
longDescription: A simple image gallery built with vanilla HTML, CSS, and JavaScript. Searches for anime images using the yande.re public API. Features search by character name, anime name, and tags. Archived because the yande.re API now requires server-side access and no longer works from the browser.
highlights: Search by character name, anime name, and tags

name: Angular Marvel Database
shortDescription: Angular app for browsing Marvel characters, comics, events, and series via the Marvel API. *(archived — API discontinued)*
longDescription: Angular application that connected to the Marvel public API to display characters, comics, creators, series, and events. Featured search and category browsing. Archived because the Marvel public API was discontinued.
highlights: Characters, comics, events, and series browsing

name: NoteNow
shortDescription: SvelteKit note-taking app with auth, workspaces, and page-based notes -- a course project I archived.
longDescription: A note-taking application built with SvelteKit following a Udemy course, extended with full authentication (email/password + GitHub OAuth via Better Auth), workspace organization, and page-based notes. Uses Drizzle ORM with PostgreSQL running in Docker for persistent storage. Archived because it was a course project rather than an original build, though it taught me advanced Svelte/SvelteKit patterns, authentication flows, transactional emails, and database setup.
highlights: User authentication with email/password and GitHub OAuth via Better Auth
Drizzle ORM with PostgreSQL via Docker
Archived -- course project, not an original build
